uncited: It sets itself apart from the [Null-Scattering Path Integral Framework](3070-null-scattering-path-integral-framework.md) by avoiding null-scattering rejection and instead analytically approximating the integral via a WKB expansion around the MPP.
- The Most Probable Path (MPP) for a given boundary condition (typically single-sided: fixed start point and direction, e.g., eye position and viewing ray).
- The action function $A(\text{path})$ associated with the light transport equation.
Identify the Most Probable Path (MPP) for the specified boundary condition.
Perform a Taylor series expansion of the action $A(\vec{\xi})$ around $\vec{\xi} = \vec{0}$.
Since $A$ has a global minimum at the MPP, the linear term is zero.
Substitute the expanded action into the path integral weight $\exp(-A(\text{path}))$.
Evaluate the integral over the re-parameterized path space.

It shows the scalar case A(ξ) = A(0) + (1/2)ξ² (∂²A/∂ξ²) + ... and then generalizes to the vector case ξ, stating that the integral involves the term (ξ ∇_ξ)² A. In the context of a multivariate Taylor expansion where the linear term is omitted due to the minimum at the MPP, the quadratic term involves the second derivatives with respect to the vector components ξ_i and ξ_j. These second derivatives constitute the Hessian matrix. Therefore, the evidence supports the definition of the Hessian matrix elements as the second partial derivatives of A with respect to ξ.
